nodes.name: build
nodes.raw: "build": "bun build bin/cine.ts --target=node --packages=external --outfile dist/cine.js && bun build src/mcp/server.ts --target=node --packages=external --outfile dist/mcp.js && bun run scripts/fix-shebang.mjs"

nodes.name: prepublishOnly
nodes.raw: "prepublishOnly": "bun run build && bun test && bun run type-check && bun run lint"

writeBoundary.producer: bun's test runner process exit code, over 11 real test files in tests/
writeBoundary.argument: The signal is the exit status of `bun test` executing tests/*.test.ts in a child process. The author writes the assertions but cannot write the verdict: a thrown TypeError or a wrong return value from src/lib/booking.ts produces a non-zero exit regardless of intent. Critically, this script is NOT orphaned the way most hackathon test scripts are — `prepublishOnly` chains `bun test`, and the package manager invokes that lifecycle hook unconditionally on publish, so the edge has a real invoker on the publish path. It has NO invoker on the merge path: there is no .github/workflows, no CI config, and no repo-tracked git hook, so a push to main is gated by nothing. Oracle caveat per the deep limit: assertions in tests/format.test.ts, tests/booking.test.ts etc. were plausibly co-authored with src/, so execution independence holds while specification independence does not.

evidence: package.json scripts.prepublishOnly = 'bun run build && bun test && bun run type-check && bun run lint'
tests/ contains 11 files: banner, booking, cache, format, mappers, member-session, order-service, search, seat-map, session-capture, token

writeBoundary.argument: tsc performs deterministic static analysis of the source and emits diagnostics the author cannot author around without changing the types themselves. The compiler binary comes from devDependencies (typescript ^5.6.0) and is not repo-modifiable code. Same invoker story as `test`: reachable through prepublishOnly, unreachable from any merge-time gate because no CI exists. Note the scope limit — this proves type consistency, not behaviour.

writeBoundary.producer: the Biome binary (@biomejs/biome ^1.9.0) in check mode, exit code driven by rule violations
writeBoundary.argument: `biome check .` without --write only reports; a violation is a non-zero exit produced by an external analyzer the source cannot influence except by conforming. biome.json enables the `recommended` rule set, which includes correctness/suspicious rules (unreachable code, unused bindings), so this is not purely cosmetic. The author can weaken it by editing biome.json — but that is a change to the rule set, not a write to the signal, so the boundary holds. Narrowness caveat: it asserts conformance to a rule list, never that the CLI books a cinema seat correctly. Invoked only via prepublishOnly; nothing invokes it on push.

evidence: biome.json files.ignore excludes data/, dist/, node_modules/, tmpclaude-*

writeBoundary.producer: the package manager's lifecycle runner, aggregating exit codes of bun build, bun test, tsc, and biome
writeBoundary.argument: This is the only automated invoker in the entire repository. npm/bun run prepublishOnly as a mandatory step of `publish` and abort the publish on non-zero exit; the author does not get to skip it in the normal path. Descending rather than trusting the wrapper: of its four children, `build` asserts nothing (bundling), while `test`, `type-check` and `lint` each terminate in an external producer traced above — so the aggregate inherits a real, falsifiable signal rather than wrapping unknowns. Two honest limits: the gate fires at publish time, not at merge or push time, so main can hold broken code indefinitely; and `--ignore-scripts` bypasses it entirely.

evidence: package.json scripts.prepublishOnly = 'bun run build && bun test && bun run type-check && bun run lint'
package.json bin { cine, cine-mcp } and files[] — this is a package intended for npm distribution
no .github/workflows, no CI config anywhere in the tree

writeBoundary.producer: Cine Colombia's live production API (token scrape -> theatres -> films -> showtimes -> seat layout), observed through scripts/smoke.ts
writeBoundary.argument: The producer side is the strongest anchor in the repository: a live third-party ticketing backend the author demonstrably cannot write to, exercised end-to-end, with real failure paths (`throw new Error('La cartelera vino vacía')`). What I cannot establish is the edge. Nothing invokes this script — it is absent from prepublishOnly, there is no CI, no tracked hook, and the file header explicitly says 'Run with `bun run scripts/smoke.ts`', i.e. a human decides both when it runs and whether its mostly-console.log output looked right. An external signal that only reaches a human eyeball on request is a diagnostic, not a gate, and I cannot trace it to any transition it blocks. Fails closed rather than crediting the repo for an anchor nothing consumes.

evidence: scripts/smoke.ts:2 'End-to-end smoke check against the live Cine Colombia API'
scripts/smoke.ts — output is console.log narrative; only one hard assertion (`if (!firstFilm) throw`)

writeBoundary.producer: bun's bundler writing dist/cine.js and dist/mcp.js, then scripts/fix-shebang.mjs
writeBoundary.argument: Produces artifacts; asserts nothing about correctness. Bun's bundler strips TypeScript types rather than checking them, so a type error that `tsc --noEmit` would catch passes through this step silently. It can fail on a syntax error or a missing import, but that is the transpiler declining to emit, not a verdict about behaviour. Excluded from the ratio.

evidence: package.json scripts.build = 'bun build bin/cine.ts ... && bun build src/mcp/server.ts ... && bun run scripts/fix-shebang.mjs'
type-check exists as a separate script precisely because build does not type-check

writeBoundary.producer: the bun runtime executing the CLI entrypoint bin/cine.ts interactively
writeBoundary.argument: Starts the interactive Clack-prompt CLI for a human to use. There is no assertion, no expected output, no pass/fail semantics — the exit code reflects whether a person quit the program. Excluded from the ratio.

writeBoundary.producer: a long-running stdio MCP server process (src/mcp/server.ts)
writeBoundary.argument: A server launcher, matching the stdio entry in .mcp.json. It runs until killed; it has no terminating success condition and therefore no verdict to emit. Excluded from the ratio.

writeBoundary.producer: Biome in --write mode, rewriting source files in place
writeBoundary.argument: The --write flag converts the diagnostic into an edit: violations are repaired rather than reported, so the step succeeds precisely because it changed the code. A step that resolves its own failure condition cannot carry information about the state it found. Excluded from the ratio; the reporting twin `lint` is where the signal lives.

writeBoundary.producer: Biome's formatter writing files in place
writeBoundary.argument: Pure rewrite — reindents to biome.json's 2-space / 100-column / single-quote settings and exits zero. It cannot fail on anything the author cares about, so it asserts nothing. Excluded from the ratio.

evidence: biome.json formatter { indentStyle: space, indentWidth: 2, lineWidth: 100 }

writeBoundary.producer: nothing — this is declarative configuration, not an executed edge
writeBoundary.argument: biome.json parameterises the `lint` and `format` edges; it does not run and emits no signal. Judging it separately would double-count the Biome edges already judged. Excluded from the ratio as a non-edge.

evidence: biome.json is a $schema-bearing config document with no executable content
